# [Feat] [Intel] lora: Add intel_xpu LoRA backend

## Motivation

On Intel XPU, multi-LoRA serving currently has to use the generic `triton`, `csgmv`, or `torch_native` backends. This PR adds an `intel_xpu` LoRA backend that runs the native Intel XPU LoRA kernels from [sgl-kernel-xpu](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu) on both the prefill and decode paths.

Usage:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path <base-model> \
    --device xpu \
    --enable-lora \
    --lora-paths <name>=<adapter-path> \
    --lora-backend intel_xpu
```

## Dependency: sgl-kernel-xpu

The backend imports these ops from `sgl_kernel` (sgl-kernel-xpu):

| Op | Used for | PR (merged and closed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embedding_lora_a_fwd` | Embedding LoRA A | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#207](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/207) |
| `sgemm_lora_a_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#262](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/262) |
| `sgemm_lora_b_fwd` | LoRA B expand, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/356) |
| `qkv_lora_b_fwd` | Fused QKV LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/393) |
| `gate_up_lora_b_fwd` | Fused gate/up LoRA B, prefill | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#490](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/490) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_fwd` | LoRA A shrink, decode | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#506](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/506) |
| `chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_fwd` | LoRA B expand, decode (single, QKV, and gate/up slices) | [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#523](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/523) |
| | LoRA kernels are optimized |  [sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#550](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/550) |

## Modifications

**New backend**: `python/sglang/srt/lora/backend/intel_xpu_backend.py` (`IntelXpuLoRABackend`)
- Prefill (contiguous batch metadata, `permutation is None`): per-shape XPU kernels (`sgemm_lora_a_fwd`, `sgemm_lora_b_fwd`, `qkv_lora_b_fwd`, `gate_up_lora_b_fwd`).
- Decode: tokens are sorted by adapter (`compute_sgemm_routing`), and the chunked-SGMV shrink/expand pair are gather fused DPAS kernels. The shrink output layout `(num_tokens, num_slices * max_rank)` is exactly the expand's input, so decode stays on XPU from A to B. The expand fuses per-adapter scaling and the `base_output` residual.
- Supports decode and prefill graph capture (`supports_prefill_cuda_graph = True`, 32 fixed prefill segment slots). Batches with more requests fall back to eager prefill.
- Batch preparation (segment routing, lm_head pruning, graph metadata) follows the triton backend's `LoRABatchInfo` layout.

**Registration and CLI**
- `lora/backend/lora_registry.py`: register `intel_xpu`.
- `arg_groups/choices.py`: add `LORA_BACKEND_CHOICES` (including `intel_xpu`). `arg_groups/fields/lora.py` now reads `--lora-backend` choices from it instead of a hardcoded list, and `server_args.py` re-exports it with the other choice lists.

**Validation**
- `arg_groups/validation_hook.py`: `validate_device_lora_backend` rejects `--lora-backend intel_xpu` without `--device xpu` at argument-check time. Without it, the error only appears later as an import failure inside `LoRAManager` init. This mirrors the existing `--sampling-backend intel_xpu` check.

**Tests**
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: `TestIntelXpuLoRABackend` (CPU CI) checks that the backend is registered and selectable from the CLI, rejected off XPU, and accepted on XPU.
- `test/manual/lora/test_lora_xpu_basics.py`: add `intel_xpu` to `DENSE_BACKENDS`, so it runs the HF+PEFT logprob comparison and the multi-LoRA batching / drainer routing tests next to `triton`, `csgmv`, and `torch_native`.

## Accuracy Tests

Models and adapters are the ones defined for `test/manual/lora/test_lora_backend.py`. Each case runs 4 engines (SRT+LoRA, SRT base, HF+LoRA, HF base) with `--lora-backend intel_xpu` and compares top input/output logprobs against HF plus ROUGE-L of the decoded text. fp16, `max_new_tokens=32`, 2 prompts per case (values are prompt 0 / prompt 1); limits: logprob diff `< 1e-1`, ROUGE-L `1.0`.

| Base model | Adapter | Max prefill logprob diff | Max decode logprob diff | ROUGE-L |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | nvidia/llama-3.1-nemoguard-8b-topic-control | 0.0155 / 0.0339 | 0.0310 / 0.0234 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Llama-2-7b-hf | winddude/wizardLM-LlaMA-LoRA-7B | 0.0161 / 0.0312 | 0.0310 / 0.0312 | 1.0 / 1.0 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | algoprog/fact-generation-llama-3.1-8b-instruct-lora | 0.0177 / 0.0312 | 0.0312 / 0.0301 | 1.0 / 1.0 | 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct

**Setup**
- Model: `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`, `--tp-size 8` on 8 Intel XPU cards, `--dtype bfloat16`, `--attention-backend triton`, `--disable-radix-cache`, graph capture on.
- LoRA: 4 bf16 adapters (`adamkarvonen/llama3.3_70b_shuffled_e3_v2`, `jeongseokoh/llama3.3_70b_sft`, `jeongseokoh/llama3.3_70b_speed60_bos`, `vineetdaniels/llama33_70b_icd_cpt`), `--max-loras-per-batch 4`, adapters drawn uniformly per request. `base` is the same model served with LoRA disabled.
- Client: SGLang serving benchmark, random dataset with lengths pinned (`--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `ignore_eos` on, so every request emits exactly `output_len` tokens), request rate inf, fixed concurrency. Every run completed all requests with exactly `num_requests * output_len` generated tokens.

**prefill_4k_4lora**: 512 in / 8 out, 128 requests, concurrency 8, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--max-running-requests 8`

| Backend | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base (no LoRA) | 1547.27 | 2014.09 | 2290.23 | 2681.61 |
| `csgmv` | 1145.49 | 2849.50 | 3163.06 | 3618.87 |
| `triton` | 1121.21 | 2915.09 | 3210.81 | 3694.60 |
| `intel_xpu`* | **1295.14** | **2337.53** | **2881.13** | **3203.76** |

`intel_xpu` vs `csgmv`: total throughput +13.1%, mean TTFT -18.0%.

**decode_128_4lora**: 16 in / 64 out, 3000 requests, concurrency 128, `--max-running-requests 128`

| Backend | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) |

| `csgmv` | 833.90 | 675.56 | 163.75 | 178.60 | 1578.59 | 11894.63 |

| `intel_xpu`* | **979.72** | **793.69** | **124.45** | **146.70** | 2299.36 | **10139.78** |

`intel_xpu` vs `csgmv`: total throughput +17.5%, mean TPOT -24.0%.

**mixed_1k_4lora**: 1024 in / 128 out, 400 requests, concurrency 20, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--max-running-requests 20`

| Backend | Total tok/s | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | P99 TPOT (ms) | Mean E2E (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `intel_xpu` | **967.28** | **107.57** | **8010.22** | **124.29** | **181.46** | **23795.51** |

`intel_xpu` vs `csgmv`: total throughput +22.0%, mean TPOT -21.2%, mean TTFT -11.1%.

**Cost of attaching adapters**. Each row is the LoRA run relative to the same base model served with no adapters, so a negative throughput delta is the expected price of LoRA.

| Scenario | Backend | Δ total throughput vs base | Δ mean E2E latency vs base |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prefill_4k_4lora | `csgmv` | −26.0 % | +35.0 % |
| prefill_4k_4lora | `triton` | −27.5 % | +37.8 % |
| prefill_4k_4lora | `intel_xpu` | **−16.3 %** | **+19.5 %** |
| decode_128_4lora | `csgmv` | −34.5 % | +52.5 % |
| decode_128_4lora | `triton` | −37.4 % | +59.6 % |
| decode_128_4lora | `intel_xpu` | **−23.1 %** | **+30.0 %** |

| mixed_1k_4lora | `intel_xpu` | **−16.0 %** | **+19.0 %** |

In `prefill_4k_4lora` each request emits only 8 tokens, so mean TPOT is dominated by decode steps queued behind other requests' prefill chunks (the base run shows the same effect: P99 ITL 1888 ms); total throughput and TTFT are the meaningful metrics there.

In `decode_128_4lora`, mean TTFT is higher with `intel_xpu` than with `csgmv` (2299 vs 1579 ms, +46 %). Each request has a 16-token prompt, so TTFT there is mostly time spent queueing for a slot in the full decode batch rather than prefill compute (base TTFT also grows with concurrency), and it is 23 % of `intel_xpu`'s end-to-end latency. Mean E2E latency is still 15 % lower than `csgmv`'s (10140 vs 11895 ms); total throughput, TPOT, and E2E latency are the meaningful metrics for decode scenarios.

The base (no-LoRA) path is unchanged by this PR: it only adds the `intel_xpu` LoRA backend, its `--lora-backend` choice, and the `--device xpu` check.

+import dataclasses
+from typing import List, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+# Native Intel XPU LoRA kernels (from sgl-kernel-xpu). Aliased with an `xpu_`
+# prefix to keep the kernel family explicit at each call site.
+from sgl_kernel import (
+    chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_fwd as xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_forward,
+)
+from sgl_kernel import (
+    chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_fwd as xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_forward,
+)
+from sgl_kernel import embedding_lora_a_fwd as xpu_embedding_lora_a_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import gate_up_lora_b_fwd as xpu_gate_up_lora_b_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import qkv_lora_b_fwd as xpu_qkv_lora_b_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import sgemm_lora_a_fwd as xpu_sgemm_lora_a_fwd
+from sgl_kernel import sgemm_lora_b_fwd as xpu_sgemm_lora_b_fwd
+
+from sglang.srt.lora.backend.triton_backend import TritonLoRABackend
+from sglang.srt.lora.utils import LoRABatchInfo
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardBatch
+
+
+class IntelXpuLoRABackend(TritonLoRABackend):
+    """LoRA on native Intel XPU kernels: per-shape sgemm kernels for contiguous prefill,
+    chunked-SGMV (gather/GEMM/scatter by permutation) for adapter-sorted decode."""
+
+    name = "intel_xpu"
+    # Triton's DP-attention global routing has no XPU kernel path.
+    supports_dp_attention = False
+    supports_prefill_cuda_graph = True
+    # sgl-kernel-xpu LoRA kernels ignore lora_ranks for the GEMM extent.
+    uses_max_rank_spaced_lora_layout = True
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _is_permuted(batch_info: LoRABatchInfo) -> bool:
+        """True when the batch metadata is adapter-sorted (decode), in which
+        case the contiguous-only XPU kernels cannot be used."""
+        return batch_info.permutation is not None
+
+    def _lora_a_shrink(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        sgemm_info: LoRABatchInfo,
+        stack_num: int,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """LoRA A shrink: sgemm_lora_a_fwd on prefill, chunked-SGMV on decode (no
+        max_chunk_size needed). Output is always in physical token order."""
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            return xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_shrink_forward(
+                input_x=x,
+                weights=weights,
+                stack_num=stack_num,
+                num_segments=sgemm_info.num_segments,
+                seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+                weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+                lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+                permutation=sgemm_info.permutation,
+            )
+        return xpu_sgemm_lora_a_fwd(
+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            stack_num=stack_num,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+        )
+
+    def _lora_b_expand(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        sgemm_info: LoRABatchInfo,
+        slice_offsets: torch.Tensor,
+        max_slice_size: int,
+        num_slices: int,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Chunked-SGMV B expand for any slice count; permutation=None on prefill.
+        Takes the shrink's (num_tokens, num_slices * max_rank) output as-is."""
+        return xpu_chunked_sgmv_lora_expand_forward(
+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            slice_offsets=slice_offsets,
+            max_slice_size=max_slice_size,
+            num_slices=num_slices,
+            num_segments=sgemm_info.num_segments,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            permutation=sgemm_info.permutation,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    # ---- LoRA kernel entry points ----
+
+    def run_lora_a_embedding(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        vocab_size: int,
+        extra_embeddings: torch.Tensor = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # self.batch_info is always contiguous (permutation=None) for
+        # embeddings, so the XPU kernel always applies.
+        bi = self.batch_info
+        assert bi is not None, (
+            "LoRA kernel invoked with no prepared batch (DP-attention idle "
+            "forward?). Gate the caller on lora_active."
+        )
+        return xpu_embedding_lora_a_fwd(
+            input_ids=input_ids,
+            weights=weights,
+            vocab_size=vocab_size,
+            seg_indptr=bi.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=bi.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=bi.lora_ranks,
+            extra_embeddings=extra_embeddings,
+            seg_lens=bi.seg_lens,
+            max_len=bi.max_len,
+        )
+
+    def run_lora_a_sgemm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        pruned_batch_info: LoRABatchInfo = None,
+        stack_num: int = 1,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info(pruned_batch_info)
+        return self._lora_a_shrink(x, weights, sgemm_info, stack_num)
+
+    def run_lora_b_sgemm(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        weights: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        pruned_batch_info: LoRABatchInfo = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info(pruned_batch_info)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): single-slice chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=x,
+                weights=weights,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=weights.shape[-2],
+                num_slices=1,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )

+            input_x=x,
+            weights=weights,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    def run_qkv_lora(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        qkv_lora_a: torch.Tensor,
+        qkv_lora_b: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        max_qkv_out_dim: int,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        n_slices: int = 3,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+
+        # x: (s, input_dim), qkv_lora_a: (num_lora, n_slices * r, input_dim),
+        # qkv_lora_b: (num_lora, total_output_dim, r)
+        assert isinstance(qkv_lora_b, torch.Tensor)
+
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info()
+        # A-shrink runs on XPU on both paths (chunked-SGMV on the permuted
+        # decode); its output is in physical token order.
+        lora_a_output = self._lora_a_shrink(x, qkv_lora_a, sgemm_info, n_slices)
+        # qkv_lora_b_fwd is fixed at 3 slices; MLA fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa has 2.
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info) or n_slices != 3:
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=lora_a_output,
+                weights=qkv_lora_b,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=max_qkv_out_dim,
+                num_slices=n_slices,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+
+        # Prefill (contiguous): XPU B-expand.
+        return xpu_qkv_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=lora_a_output,
+            qkv_lora_b=qkv_lora_b,
+            output_offset=output_offset,
+            max_qkv_out_dim=max_qkv_out_dim,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    def run_gate_up_lora(
+        self,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        gate_up_lora_a: torch.Tensor,
+        gate_up_lora_b: torch.Tensor,
+        output_offset: torch.Tensor,
+        base_output: torch.Tensor = None,
+        *args,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+
+        # x: (s, input_dim), gate_up_lora_a: (num_lora, 2 * r, input_dim),
+        # gate_up_lora_b: (num_lora, 2 * output_dim, r)
+        assert isinstance(gate_up_lora_b, torch.Tensor)
+        output_dim = gate_up_lora_b.shape[-2] // 2
+
+        sgemm_info = self._sgemm_info()
+        # A-shrink runs on XPU on both paths (chunked-SGMV on the permuted
+        # decode); its output is in physical token order.
+        lora_a_output = self._lora_a_shrink(x, gate_up_lora_a, sgemm_info, 2)
+        if self._is_permuted(sgemm_info):
+            # Decode (permuted): fused 2-way (gate, up) chunked-SGMV expand on XPU.
+            return self._lora_b_expand(
+                x=lora_a_output,
+                weights=gate_up_lora_b,
+                sgemm_info=sgemm_info,
+                slice_offsets=output_offset,
+                max_slice_size=output_dim,
+                num_slices=2,
+                base_output=base_output,
+            )
+
+        # Prefill (contiguous): XPU B-expand.
+        return xpu_gate_up_lora_b_fwd(
+            input_x=lora_a_output,
+            gate_up_lora_b=gate_up_lora_b,
+            output_dim=output_dim,
+            seg_indptr=sgemm_info.seg_indptr,
+            weight_indices=sgemm_info.weight_indices,
+            lora_ranks=sgemm_info.lora_ranks,
+            scalings=sgemm_info.scalings,
+            seg_lens=sgemm_info.seg_lens,
+            base_output=base_output,
+        )
+
+    def _prepare_prefill_cuda_graph_sgemm_batch_info(
+        self, forward_batch: ForwardBatch, weight_indices: List[int]

+        # XPU kernels tile M per segment; fixed-size chunks only add partial tiles.

+        """Sort tokens by adapter and build merged segments for sgemm LoRA."""
+        bi = self.batch_info

+                use_cuda_graph=False,
+                num_segments=mlpb,

The XPU kernels deliberately contract over the full max_rank, so the backend now declares uses_max_rank_spaced_lora_layout and the pool places each stacked A slice at p * max_lora_rank, matching what MoE A already does.
